pull.title: refactor: break the blockstorage/validation circular dependency
pull.body:
`node/blockstorage.cpp` includes `validation.h`, and the lint lists `node/blockstorage -> validation -> node/blockstorage` as an expected circular dependency. This removes it, and the lint confirms the cycle is gone.

The largest user of validation in block storage is `ImportBlocks`, which drives validation. It moves to `node/chainstate` and sets the reindex flag through the new `BlockManager::SetBlockfilesIndexed()`, which writes the flag to the block tree database and sets the in-memory flag under one `cs_main` hold. The last commit moves `FatalError` to `kernel/fatal_error.h`, after which `blockstorage.cpp` no longer includes `validation.h`. `validation.h` still exports `FatalError` for its other users.

Validation also reaches into `BlockManager`'s private members as a friend. `RequestPrune()` and `MarkBlockIndexDirty()` replace the friend declarations, keeping `m_check_for_pruning` and `m_dirty_blockindex` non-public. Both require `cs_main`, and the annotations let the compiler check it. After this, nothing outside `BlockManager` writes its private state or the block tree database.

There is no behavior change to my knowledge.

Based on #36738. Draft until it is merged.

Thanks to musaHaruna, who [suggested `RequestPrune()`](https://github.com/pzafonte/bitcoin/pull/2#discussion_r4283138022) in his review on my fork. The flag marks a pending pruning check, so callers request it and storage decides whether anything qualifies, which keeps the flag private once the friend declarations are gone.

validation: delete pruned files on a later flush

Files selected for pruning were kept in a local, so a failed flush left
them on disk until the next startup.

Keep them in BlockManager and delete them after the next block index
write. Take them with the dirty entries, which WriteBlockIndexDB() drops
even if the write fails. Drop a file from the set once a block is
written to it.

Pending files wait for the next periodic, forced or shutdown flush
rather than forcing one, which would retry a failing write on every
block.

refactor: move prune bookkeeping into BlockManager

Move FlushStateToDisk's handling of the prune request, prune locks,
pruned flag, files to delete and blocks directory space check into
BlockManager. The prune request is cleared before the prune locks are
applied rather than after selection, which differs only if selection
throws.

An Assume checks that the pruned flag is set before files are queued
for deletion, so a restart knows blocks were deleted.
